records.title: No way to drive one client of a multi-client play session (high)
records.reported_title: No way to drive one client of a multi-client play session (high)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Limitation.
- **Scenario:** A play session with three standalone local clients in one editor process.
- **Reproduction status:** Observed once.
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Start a play session with three clients.
  2. Try to send a key or a console command to client two only.
- **Observed:** The play input tools refuse when more than one play world exists. The diagnostic console tool accepts only log and console-variable commands, not general console commands. No other tool sends input or a console command to one client.
- **Expected:** A way to target one play instance for input and for a console command. Basis: user expectation for local multiplayer tests.
- **Impact:** Blocked workflow. The user had to press keys and type commands by hand in each client window.
- **State after:** No change.
- **Workaround:** Manual input by the user. Not completed in this session.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** See FT-142.
records.remaining: Design explicit stable world/client targeting and read-back; retain ambiguity refusal. General console execution is a separate capability/safety decision, not an implied widening of diagnostic commands.

records.title: Function rename refused for a widget used by two hosts (medium)
records.reported_title: Function rename refused for a widget used by two hosts (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Limitation.
- **Scenario:** Rename of five functions in a widget Blueprint that two host widgets contain.
- **Reproduction status:** Repeated, 5 of 5.
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Compile the widget clean.
  2. Call EditTurboMCPFunctionRename on any of its functions.
- **Observed:** Refused with "More than 256 dependent packages require inspection". Nothing renamed.
- **Expected:** The rename succeeds when the direct callers are few, or the tool scans only real callers. Basis: user expectation.
- **Impact:** Each rename became create new function, copy body, delete old function. About 20 extra calls.
- **State after:** Unchanged.
- **Workaround:** New functions plus EditTurboMCPGraphCopy. Worked, with GC-97.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** Count only packages that reference the function, not all dependents of the asset.
records.remaining: Reconcile current source and help, then reproduce before implementing a bounded repair.

records.observation:
- **Type:** Usability.

  2. Call PreviewTurboMCPGraphTidy with only the parameters that the help shows.

The first call was refused for a missing required parameter. The same thing happened with the other three tools.
- **Expected:** Compact help always lists every required parameter, even when it shortens descriptions.

records.title: Tidy spreads loop continuations as a staircase of rows across the full width (medium)
records.reported_title: Tidy spreads loop continuations as a staircase of rows across the full width (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Defect.
- **Scenario:** Appendix A. Two loops in sequence, a nested loop, a fallback that rejoins at a merge node.
- **Reproduction status:** Observed once in preview.
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Call PreviewTurboMCPGraphTidy on the whole graph: empty node list, empty main path, empty wrap points, bForce false, default gaps.
  2. Open the before and after preview images.
- **Observed:** Each loop body and the branch True path stayed on the row of their control node. Each Completed path and the False path moved one row lower and far to the right. The real flow went down in a staircase over three rows that spanned the whole width, joined by long diagonal exec wires. The user marked three crossing exec paths on the image and rejected the layout.
- **Expected:** Rules R2 to R6 in Appendix C. Keeping the body on the row is correct. The defect is the global placement: blocks are not compact rectangles, Completed blocks are not placed below their loop, and handoff wires are diagonal.
- **Impact:** The layout could not be accepted. One agent pass and one user hand pass were needed.
- **State after:** Preview only. No change to the asset.
- **Workaround:** Exact positions with EditTurboMCPGraphPositions, then a hand correction by the user. This worked.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** FT-149 and FT-150.
records.remaining: Keep Body and True on their control row; Completed below its body; inner Completed inside outer body. Preserve feedback and merge semantics. Never implement withdrawn Completed-on-main-row rule.

records.title: Rejected hypothesis: Completed on the main row (medium)
records.reported_title: Rejected hypothesis: Completed on the main row (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Proposal, withdrawn.
- **Scenario:** Same as TD-62.
- **Reproduction status:** Tested once as the agent layout (output B in Appendix B).
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Place every loop's Completed path on one straight main row and the loop bodies in lanes below.
  2. Show the result to the user.
- **Observed:** The agent first read the TD-62 crossings as "the wrong output stays on the row" and built output B on that idea. The user rated it better than the default but corrected it by hand. The user's reference keeps the body on the row and drops Completed below.
- **Expected:** An agent that improves the tool must not implement "Completed on the main row." FT-145 is withdrawn for the same reason.
- **Impact:** One full layout pass built on a wrong rule.
- **State after:** Superseded by the user reference.
- **Workaround:** Not applicable.
- **Cause:** The agent inferred the rule from the crossings without a reference layout.
- **Proposed behavior:** Before changing a layout rule, compare against a user reference layout. Appendix F gives a way to build one.
records.remaining: Preserve observation; not a new fix.

records.reported_title: Tidy has no option to cache reused values in locals (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Proposal.
- **Scenario:** One pure call output feeds three consumers across two loop levels. One impure call output feeds three consumers at the far end, including the fallback.
- **Reproduction status:** Observed once.
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Preview the tidy and read the getter-split count.
  2. Call PreviewTurboMCPGraphSplitValue on the pure call.
- **Observed:** The tidy split 0 getters and kept the long data wires. The split tool refused the pure call because it accepts only getters and literals.
- **Expected:** Rule R7.
- **Impact:** 2 locals, 2 setters and 6 getters created by the agent with one append.
- **State after:** Compiled clean.
- **Workaround:** EditTurboMCPLocalVariableAdd, then EditTurboMCPGraphAppend with explicit rewiring. This worked.
- **Cause:** Not applicable.
- **Proposed behavior:** FT-152.
records.remaining: Candidate report first; promotion explicitly selected and separate from geometry. Prove evaluation timing, dominance and loop frequency preservation; refuse unsafe caching. Do not automatically cache arbitrary pure expressions.
